thread.title: Facebook Smart Speakers Focus On Video Calling | Investor's Business Daily

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Facebook Smart Speakers Focus On Video Calling | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Facebook ( FB ) on Monday jumped into the booming market for smart speakers with two devices that put an emphasis on video-based calling.
X Facebook is a late entrant in a market led by Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and its Echo line of smart speakers. Another player is Alphabet ( GOOGL ), with its Google Home device. In third is Apple ( AAPL ).
According to research firm Strategy Analytics, the smart-speaker market is worth $6.7 billion in 2018. That will grow to $23.5 billion by 2023, it says.
The smaller of the two Facebook smart speakers, called Portal, costs $199 and includes a 10-inch video display. It's similar to the Amazon Echo Show. The larger version, called Portal+, costs $349 and has a 15-inch display that can be adjusted for portrait or landscape modes.

They are the central communication hub of smart homes. In addition to providing users an encyclopedia of information, they also provide users the opportunity to control appliances and manage home security through vocal commands.
Amazon Sets The Tone Amazon set the market in motion more than three years ago by introducing the Echo, with its artificially intelligent voice assistant named Alexa. The device initially helped with common things like playing music, keeping lists and answering questions.
Preorders are now available from Facebook . Facebook offers a $100 discount for any two devices bought together. The devices also are for sale on Amazon or at Best Buy ( BBY ).
Calls go to other people with Portal devices. They also go to anyone with a smartphone or tablet with Facebook and Messenger accounts.
A key feature of the Portal+ is a wide-angle camera. It automatically keeps users in focus as they move about a room.
Records Wiped, Says Facebook The devices are hands free and mostly controlled by voice. Security features include the ability to disable the camera and microphone with a single tap.
"Facebook doesn't listen to, view, or keep the contents of your Portal video calls," said the Facebook smart speaker product announcement . "Your Portal conversations stay between you and the people you're calling. In addition, video calls on Portal are encrypted, so your calls are always secure."
For music listening, Facebook has partnered with Spotify ( SPOT ), Pandora ( P ) and iHeartRadio.
Shares of Facebook closed at 157.25, down a fraction on the stock market today .
Last month, Amazon introduced more than a dozen new Echo and Alexa-connected devices .
